messages:
alex.m: Quick heads-up — trying to onboard Caracole-13B-v2 for a low-latency rerank path. License page looks weird: mentions non-commercial use + attribution and a clause about not redistributing quantized/compiled binaries. Can legal triage? https://model-zoo.example/caracole-13b-v2

rachel.legal: Thanks — can you paste the exact clause? NC licenses typically block commercial hosting. If it forbids distribution of transformed weights, that could block Private/edge deployments where we'd ship binaries.

alex.m: Pasted excerpt:
```
Section 3.b: Redistribution of model "weights" or derivatives (including quantized, pruned, or compiled binaries) is prohibited unless separate commercial license obtained.
```

sam.k: For clarity: our Hosted/Dedicated model serving does NOT ship weights to customers — we serve from our runtime. But Private/on-prem customers expect a package or image with the quantized model, which might be redistribution.

frida: Also worried about cache/edge snapshots — does "compiled binaries" cover our optimized runtime cache? Might be interpreted broadly.

rachel.legal: Two main concerns: the NC (non-commercial) term likely prevents paid hosting; and the redistribution phrase could prevent shipping quantized artifacts. We need to ask the authors for 1) a commercial license option, and 2) whether 'derivatives' includes transform formats like quantization or runtime caches.

alex.m: Short-term: can we run internal evals and quant experiments on infra w/ no external distribution? Also, can we list the model in catalog as internal-research-only so engineers can test?

rachel.legal: Internal, private evals for research are usually okay under NC, provided we don't offer it as a paid product. Listing as "research-only" in the catalog is a good interim measure. For hosting to paying customers, we'll need explicit permission. I'll draft Qs to send to the model authors.

compliance-bot: Action created: LEG-4321. Requesting commercial licensing/addendum from Caracole maintainers. Owner: rachel.legal. ETA: 3 business days.

sam.k: If authors deny commercial rights, fallback: pick an alternative permissively licensed model (e.g., Nimbus-7B) for Dedicated/Private and keep Caracole for internal evals only.

alex.m: I'll remove Caracole from the "ready" tag in the catalog and mark it "legal-review".

rachel.legal: Thanks — I'll update this thread when we hear back. If folks want to run evaluation prompts against it in the meantime, use the internal eval cluster only and avoid sharing artifacts externally.
